facts: I've submitted 15 pull requests to Godot Engine — 6 merged, 7 open, and 2 closed — across editor, GUI, GDScript, and web platform areas.
I built SXSHELL, a modular Unix-like shell in C with 7 modules (~550 lines), pipelines, I/O redirection, and POSIX system calls.
My E-Commerce Backend API implements transactional order processing with concurrency-safe inventory reservation.
The API Rate Limiter uses Redis-backed Token Bucket algorithm with atomic Lua scripts for concurrent request handling.
I maintain an 8.84 CGPA in my BCA degree at Amity University Online alongside Harvard CS50x and CS50 SQL certifications.
One of my Godot Engine regression fixes (#124170, script editor tooltip positioning) was merged 33 hours after submission.
Working across Java Spring Boot, C systems programming, and open-source engine internals gives me different perspectives on software design.

projects.title: What I've built
projects.intro: Two Java backend applications, a systems programming project, and open-source contributions to a large C++ codebase.

items.title: E-Commerce Backend API
items.description: An e-commerce backend built with Java and Spring Boot, providing REST APIs for product management, shopping carts, orders, and user accounts, with PostgreSQL persistence and secure authentication.
items.learning: Layered controller-service-repository architecture with transactional order processing and concurrency-safe inventory reservation.
underTheHood: Layered REST API architecture with DTO-based request/response handling, validation, and centralized exception handling
Spring Security with JWT authentication, password hashing, and role-based authorization for protected endpoints
Spring Data JPA with Hibernate, Flyway migrations, relational entity relationships, and database constraints
Transactional inventory reservation with locking-based concurrency control to prevent overselling under simultaneous requests
JUnit 5 and Mockito for service-layer testing, integration tests, and transaction consistency verification

items.title: API Rate Limiter & Usage Metering Service
items.description: A Redis-backed API rate-limiting service using the Token Bucket algorithm to enforce configurable per-user and per-API-key request limits, with usage metering and concurrency-safe request handling.
items.learning: Backend infrastructure and algorithmic engineering — not a CRUD application, but a service focused on algorithms, atomic operations, concurrency, and HTTP behaviour.
underTheHood: Token Bucket algorithm with configurable request limits, per-user and per-API-key restrictions, and controlled burst handling
Redis-backed rate-limit state with TTL-based expiration and atomic Lua scripts for concurrent request handling
HTTP 429 Too Many Requests responses, Retry-After headers, rate-limit headers, and usage metering
JUnit 5 and Mockito for boundary tests, expiration tests, and concurrent-burst test scenarios

items.title: SXSHELL — Unix-like Shell
items.description: A modular Unix-like shell implemented in C, with command parsing, process execution, pipelines, and I/O redirection using POSIX system calls.
items.learning: Demonstrates systems programming fundamentals — process management, file descriptors, and low-level command execution.
underTheHood: Seven modules (~550 lines) with separation of command parsing and process execution
Pipelines and I/O redirection using fork(), execv(), and dup2()
Built-in commands, executable lookup, $PATH resolution, and quote/escape parsing

about.title: About me
about.intro: I'm a BCA Computer Science student at Amity University Online with a focus on Java backend development.
approachParagraphs: My work includes building Spring Boot applications, working with PostgreSQL and Redis, and implementing backend functionality involving authentication, data persistence, transactions, and concurrency.

Alongside application development, I contribute to the Godot Engine open-source project, where I have worked on editor, GUI, and web-platform issues. I have also built SXSHELL, a Unix-like shell in C using POSIX system calls.
I'm particularly interested in backend engineering, software design, debugging, and understanding how applications behave beyond their frameworks.
